# Report information

Focused **sample-quality** report for immunopeptidomics experiments, provided by
the Immunopeptidomics Platform (IPP). It condenses several interpretable signals
into one per-sample **quality score** — how strongly each sample resembles a real
HLA immunopeptidome — inspired by the HowDirty contamination score but inverted
(goodness rather than badness).

**Sample Set:** `r params$SampleSet`

**Data Analysis: ** `r params$DataAnalysisNames`

**Date:**  `r Sys.Date()`

**Code version:** `r packageVersion("HowMaHiCo")`

```{r child = system.file("rmarkdown", "shared", "setup.Rmd", package = "HowMaHiCo")}
```


```{r quality-score-data, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=TRUE}
# Derive the QC-control sample set from the annotation QC column (optional).
qc_samples <- character(0)
if (nzchar(params$QCColumn)) {
  annot_qc <- tryCatch(
    read_annot(file.path(params$FolderDocumentation, params$AnnotationFile)),
    error = function(e) NULL)
  if (!is.null(annot_qc) && params$QCColumn %in% names(annot_qc)) {
    flag <- annot_qc[[params$QCColumn]]
    is_qc <- as.character(flag) %in% c("TRUE", "T", "1", "QC", "qc", "yes", "Yes")
    qc_samples <- unique(as.character(annot_qc$Sample[is_qc]))
  }
}

threshold_mode <- if (params$ThresholdMode == "qc_relative" && length(qc_samples) > 0)
  "qc_relative" else "default"
if (params$ThresholdMode == "qc_relative" && length(qc_samples) == 0)
  warning("ThresholdMode = 'qc_relative' but no QC samples were found; using default thresholds.")

scores <- score_sample_quality(pep_all, shortpep_range = shortpep_range,
                               mhcclass = params$MHCclass,
                               qc_samples = qc_samples,
                               threshold_mode = threshold_mode)
thresholds_used <- if (threshold_mode == "qc_relative")
  calibrate_thresholds_from_qc(qc_metrics_by_sample(pep_all, shortpep_range, params$MHCclass),
                               qc_samples) else quality_thresholds_default()
```

`r if (length(qc_samples) > 0) paste0("**QC control samples:** ", paste(qc_samples, collapse = ", "), " (marked with * in plots).") else "No QC control samples tagged (set an annotation ", "<code>", params$QCColumn, "</code> column to enable QC-relative thresholds)."`

**Threshold mode:** `r threshold_mode`

# Overview

Composite quality score (0-100) and traffic-light category per sample. The
composite is a weighted mean of the available sub-scores; dimensions that are
undefined for this dataset (e.g. anchor motifs for MHC-II, mass error for DIA-NN)
drop out instead of penalising the sample.

```{r overview-table, echo=FALSE}
overview <- scores |>
  dplyr::transmute(Sample,
                   QC = ifelse(is_QC, "QC", ""),
                   `Composite score` = composite_score,
                   Category = as.character(category))
overview |>
  kable() |>
  kable_paper("hover", full_width = FALSE)
```

# Composite scores

```{r plot-composite, echo=FALSE, fig.height=4, fig.width=8, warning=FALSE}
p_quality_composite <- plot_quality_composite(scores)
p_quality_composite
```

# Per-metric breakdown

Sub-scores (0-100) for every sample and quality dimension. Red = poor, green =
good; grey = not applicable to this dataset.

```{r plot-heatmap, echo=FALSE, fig.height=4, fig.width=8, warning=FALSE}
p_quality_heatmap <- plot_quality_heatmap(scores, thresholds_used)
p_quality_heatmap
```

## Raw metrics

The underlying raw values behind each sub-score.

```{r raw-metrics-table, echo=FALSE}
raw_cols <- intersect(thresholds_used$metric, names(scores))
scores |>
  dplyr::select(Sample, dplyr::all_of(raw_cols)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 3))) |>
  print_annot()
```

# Methods

Each dimension, its scoring direction, the thresholds in force, and its weight in
the composite. In `default` mode the green/amber thresholds are literature-informed
constants; in `qc_relative` mode green is the QC-sample median and amber is that
median relaxed by 20%.

```{r methods-table, echo=FALSE}
thresholds_used |>
  dplyr::transmute(Metric = label, Direction = direction,
                   `Green (=100)` = round(green, 3), `Amber (=50)` = round(amber, 3),
                   Weight = weight) |>
  kable() |>
  kable_paper("hover", full_width = FALSE)
```

- **Length in window / 9-mer fraction** — the hallmark of an HLA immunopeptidome:
  peptides concentrate in the expected ligand-length window (here
  `r paste0(shortpep_range[1], "-", shortpep_range[2])` AAs) and, for HLA-I, peak at 9-mers.
- **Anchor motif clarity** — Shannon information (bits) at the P2 and PΩ anchor
  positions of 9-mers; sharp anchors indicate genuine allele-restricted ligands.
  Computed from the data only (no binding predictor or HLA typing).
- **Tryptic background (long peptides)** — fraction of peptides *outside* the
  length window ending in K/R. Because some HLA-I alleles legitimately use K/R as a
  C-terminal anchor, the overall C-terminal K/R fraction is reported only as a
  low-weight diagnostic; the scored signal isolates tryptic contamination in the
  long-peptide tail.
- **Charge 1+/2+** — short HLA-I ligands ionise predominantly as 1+/2+.
- **Depth** — unique peptides / in-window peptides / source proteins; scored only
  in `qc_relative` mode (absolute yield is not comparable without per-input
  normalisation).
- **Median |ppm|** — mass accuracy; `NA` (dropped) for DIA-NN, which reports a
  dummy `ppm = 0`.

```{r export-results, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Always-written export: render parameters + the per-sample score table
write_input_params(params, folder = FolderResults, prefix = "05_quality_score")
write.csv_rawr(scores, folder = FolderResults)

if (params$PlotsSave) {
  ggsave_rawr(p_quality_composite, "p_quality_composite", folder = FolderFigures,
              width = nrow(scores) + 6, height = 10)
  ggsave_rawr(p_quality_heatmap, "p_quality_heatmap", folder = FolderFigures,
              width = nrow(scores) + 6, height = 12)
}
```
